"ראיתי אותו, חיבקתי ונישקתי אותו. הוא היה שלו ויפה, כמו תמיד. אריה, אבל אריה שישן", סיפר. ילד טבע, ספורט, אתגרים ויופי. גבר שבגברים, מלך העולם, אריה חזק שנדם. זכינו בך לעשרים שנים מאושרות. נשארת יפה, גבוה, חזק - חתיך בפער, כמו שנהגת לומר. אתה אריה, אריה שישן – אבל אריה. נלחמת עם הדר חברך מילדות נפלאה ברעים, הצלת חברים רבים, חלקם כלל לא הכרת. שלושה רימונים וכדור רובה עוצרים גם אריה. חיבקתי אותך בלילה בקיבוץ על האלונקה, ליטפתי את רעמתך השחורה ונישקתי אריה. אריה שוכב, גדול וחזק, אריה קר, גיאגו שלנו, אתה וכל הנופלים לא הלכתם לשווא, אתם זעקת ההשכמה הכואבת לאחדות בינינו. זעקה שמתחילה להתנחל בכל הלבבות, שמחברת בינינו בעצב, בשכול, בדם ובגבורה. אנחנו נקום, ננקום ונקומם את ארצנו מחדש. זה מה לא מצאתי שם אותך // כמעט שבועיים שהשמיים / ריקים כאלה, אבדה לי המנגינה / הלכת, אז גם היא הלכה איתך. // ואיך הכאב לא עובר / כדורים ופסנתר אל תוך הלילה / ואיך העולם לא קורס, הלב לא תופס / ומי יחזיר לי ת'חיבוק שלך / שלך שלך. // העיר שותקת, כבר אין לי שקט / פתאום הופעת, מטייל לי בחלומות / עם החיוך הזה והעיניים היפות. // ואיך הכאב לא עובר / כדורים ופסנתר אל תוך הלילה / ואיך העולם לא קורס, הלב לא תופס / ומי יחזיר לי ת'חיבוק שלך / שלך שלך. // ביי גיא".

Guy Simhi, the youngest son of Orit and Dedy, was born on 7 Sivan 5763 (6 June 2003) on Kibbutz Reim in the northern Negev. He had two older brothers, Tomer and Alon. Guy, known as Guyago to those close to him, grew up and was educated on Kibbutz Reim. "A natural child of the outdoors, a leader and fighter from birth, active, handsome, and charming," his mother said. "A beloved child who got all the best qualities. The kind who comes in a limited edition."

He attended the "Nitzanei Eshkol" elementary school on Kibbutz Magen. When he was six, the family moved with him to Beijing, China, after his father was appointed the IDF attaché in that country. There he studied at an international school with pupils from all over the world. He excelled in various sports, including football, swimming and rugby. On vacations he travelled with his parents and brothers within China and to neighboring countries, diving, climbing mountains and skiing down snowy slopes. When he was nine, the family returned to Israel and settled in the town of Gedera. Guy studied at the "Reut" elementary school and continued at the "Draka-Ramon" high school in the town. He quickly made new friends, both boys and girls, and became one of the leaders of his class. He was charismatic, smiling and joyful, very sociable and a lover of people. He connected children and formed groups of friends who spent time together and went to parties. He looked out for children who were less accepted socially, protected them, included them in his group and took them under his wing. He was a member of the "Maccabi Tzair" youth movement and even led groups in it. He stood out for his courage and determination and was strong in body and spirit. He was an outstanding athlete, playing basketball and volleyball. He loved the State of Israel and the Jewish people, travelled the length and breadth of the country, and prepared himself for meaningful service in the army.

On 12 August 2021 he enlisted in the IDF and served in the Paratroopers Reconnaissance Unit. He completed a squad commanders course and served as a company sergeant major at a brigade training base for about six months. He then returned to the veteran fighting team of the unit. In his commander's notebook he wrote his thoughts on command and leadership: "Sometimes you have to sacrifice yourself for the team"; "Don't be a victim of self-pity"; "A person is a person through other people"; "It's all about how much you can absorb and keep going. You can't defeat a person who gets up after every fall. Always keep moving forward." These sentences, by which he lived as a fighter and as a person, reflect resolve and strength of will, persistence and readiness to sacrifice for the collective.

On Friday, 6 October 2023, Guy was on leave from the unit and was at home in Gedera. In the evening he went with friends from the town and from his unit to the "Nova" nature festival near Kibbutz Reim. He danced, partied and enjoyed himself at the festival until dawn. On Saturday, 22 Tishri 5784, Simchat Torah, 7 October 2023, at 6:30 in the morning, the terrorist organization Hamas launched a surprise attack on Israel. Under cover of massive fire of missiles and rockets from the Gaza Strip into large areas of the country, thousands of terrorists infiltrated by land, sea and air and began a murderous assault on the communities around Gaza and on Sderot, Ofakim and Netivot, on the nature festival near Kibbutzim Reim and Nir Am, on IDF bases and on travelers on the roads in the area. The terrorists murdered some 800 civilians in their homes and in their cars, after committing grave crimes against them. They abducted hundreds of Israelis to the Gaza Strip and destroyed, looted and set fire to homes and property. Hundreds of soldiers, police officers, members of the security forces and local emergency squad members fell in battle. That morning, a war began.

When the rocket launches from Gaza began, Guy quickly took charge and led his twelve friends who had been at the party, across the fields to the nearby Kibbutz Reim, which he knew well from childhood, to find shelter in protected spaces. When they reached the kibbutz, they found refuge with a friend of Guy's, a fighter in the "Maglan" commando unit. About an hour after the first launches, dozens of terrorists infiltrated the kibbutz and shots rang out from every direction. At 7:43 Guy called his father and reported on the situation. His father told him to enter the safe room in the friend's apartment, lock the door and wait a few minutes until the army arrived. Guy made sure his friends entered the safe room, and then, despite the danger, went out to find young people who had fled the party and were hiding around the kibbutz, in bushes, in open shelters and elsewhere. He realized this was not a safe place with terrorists infiltrating. He approached the frightened young people in the shelters and said confidently, "Hi, I'm Simhi, follow me." And they followed him. For several long minutes he brought many partygoers into the safe rooms, and only then did he return to the friend's apartment. His friends were already locked in the safe room, keeping absolutely silent, and Guy waited alertly in the small living room with his friend, who was armed with a weapon. The friend begged him to go into the safe room, but he refused. "Do you think I'd leave you alone?" he said. Guy was wearing shorts, with no shirt and no weapon, but when the terrorists arrived, he became a Paratroopers Reconnaissance fighter. "We're going to kill them all," he told his friend. After a while, shouts in Arabic and bursts of gunfire were heard, coming closer. Five terrorists reached the apartment door and tried to break it open. When one of them managed to get in, Guy surprised him, jumped on him with bare hands and strangled him, apparently to death. The second terrorist who entered was shot by his friend. When the remaining terrorists realized they would not leave the apartment alive, they began throwing grenades into the living room. The friend was wounded in the leg but managed to get out through the window and climb onto the roof. Guy was seriously wounded by three grenades thrown in, managed to get out through the window, and was shot to death by a terrorist who was outside. The friends who were in the safe room in the apartment, the armed friend, and the many young people he had brought out of the shelters into protected spaces on the kibbutz all survived. Through his heroism, his resourcefulness, his sacrifice and his self-devotion, Guy saved thirty people, who are left to tell the story of the battle.

That night Guy's parents learned that he had fallen while protecting his friends. His father put on uniform and went to the kibbutz to bring his son out. "I saw him, I hugged and kissed him. He was still his beautiful self, as always. A lion, but a sleeping lion," he said. "Guy fought fearlessly for his friends and for people, some of whom he did not know at all. This spirit, the Jewish spirit, cannot be defeated, even if twenty thousand terrorists came."

Sergeant First Class Guy Simhi fell in battle on 22 Tishri 5784 (7 October 2023), aged twenty. He was laid to rest in the military section of the cemetery in Gedera. He left behind his parents and two brothers. His father Dedy eulogized him: "Our Guy, our lion. We are a family of lionesses and lion sons. A perfect child, loved, and a fighter at heart. A child of nature, sport, challenges and beauty. The most manly of men, king of the world, a strong lion who fell silent. We were blessed with you for twenty happy years. You remained handsome, tall, strong, and by far the most handsome, as you used to say. You are a lion, a sleeping lion, but a lion. You fought with the courage of your childhood friend from Reim, you saved many friends, some you did not even know. Three grenades and a rifle bullet can stop even a lion. I hugged you at night on the stretcher at the kibbutz, I stroked your black mane and kissed the lion. A lion lying down, big and strong, a cold lion, but still a lion. The country is at war, your unit's lions are fighting, and I'm sure Simhi is missed by them. Our friends in Kibbutz Reim are lions and lionesses. We will win, we are a people of lions. We have three lions at home, and we will always have three lions. One lion sleeps, and the lioness will always watch over him. We kiss you, beloved of our hearts."

His brother Alon eulogized him: "I promise to be strong and to live up to the expectations you had of me. People always said I was your role model, but my brother, look at you, you're my role model."

His aunt Adva eulogized him: "Our Guy, the most successful, the most beautiful, the funniest, the biggest hero. You fought to the last moment, and thanks to you everyone is alive."

Gali eulogized him: "It simply doesn't feel real that our best friend isn't here. We sit here every day and hope he will somehow walk through the gate. We wait for him, and it just doesn't happen."

Odelia eulogized him: "Guyago, I'm writing and I can't believe it. A child of life. A leader from birth. How much light and beauty and goodness you spread in your short life. Everyone who had the privilege of knowing you is left with a hole in their heart. We will remember and miss you forever. May your memory be blessed."

Noam eulogized him: "Thank you, Guy, for saving my girlfriend from the massacre at Nova. Thanks to you, many lives were saved. Thank you, and may your memory be blessed forever."

Pini eulogized him: "Guy, hero of Israel, when I heard you fought with bare hands in Beni Beliyal and saved many lives, it did not surprise me at all. Having grown up alongside your grandfather, a firefighter who saved many lives, I knew you belonged to the next generation of brave fighters. We are very sad that you are not with us, but you will always be in our hearts and thoughts. Loving you and embracing you forever."

At the thirtieth-day memorial, his father said: "Our hero. You fought with bare hands and saved many of your friends. For hours Mom and I have been thinking about why, but we know the answer well. It is burned into your character, it is stamped into your sculpted body. From age zero you were a fighter, a lion cub, always first. Yes, you were always a leader, a guide, the king of the lions. You and a cemetery don't go together for me. You connect with parties, beaches and nature. You are connected to joy, to love of the land, to giving, to fighting and to victories. Now we commit to connecting to all of these. We will continue to smile, to lead and to love our country just as you did. The Jewish people is a people of lions, like you. A people that unites, a people that grows stronger and a people that wins. Our Guyago, you and all the fallen did not go in vain. You are the painful wake-up call to unity among us, a cry that is beginning to take root in every heart, connecting us in sorrow, in bereavement, in blood and in heroism. We will avenge, we will avenge and we will raise our land up again. That is what you would do. The last book you read was 'Responsibility and Victory,' and that is you, and that is your testament. I pledge to you, my dear son, that it will be so. Farewell, my beloved, the love of my soul. We are not parting. We will keep walking together everywhere and always."

In memory of Guy, a Torah scroll was written, and it will travel between synagogues across the country for the unity of Israel. An account of Guy's act of heroism appears in the book "One Day in October – Forty Heroes, Forty Stories" by Yair Agmon and Oriya Mevorach (Koren Publishers, 2024). The chapter is titled "The Least Ordinary Person in the World – The Story of Guy Simhi." Guy is commemorated in the memorial corner of graduates of Draka-Ramon High School who fell or were murdered in hostile acts. Based on the letters of Guy's name, his brothers Tomer and Alon tattooed the words "Guy, my brother, hero of Israel" on their bodies, and his father tattooed "Guy, hero of Israel, lion."

On Guy's birthday, 6 June 2024, Gedera youth distributed his favorite cookies throughout the town. The "Recipe with Memory" project features the chocolate-chip cookie recipe he loved: www.instagram.com/reel/C64BZpLISv9

The Simhi family initiated a day of activities in his memory, "Heroes Create Unity" (the initials of his name), on 2 April 2024, with the participation of youth movement members and high school students in Gedera. Further commemorative initiatives include a protective vest bearing his name, "Guy's Fortress Vest," by the company Marom Dolphin; "Guyago football" and "Guyago bracelets" engraved with the phrases "Don't forget to enjoy life even in my share" and "The most Guyago by far"; and a birthday cake with elements recounting his life, from his childhood in China to his military service, made by volunteers at Viktoriacakes. Hundreds of photos and videos of Guy have been uploaded to a website in his memory: app.kululu.com/album/ygjuun. Memorial pages were posted on Instagram and TikTok: www.instagram.com/remember_guy_simhi www.instagram.com/iron.flowers2023/p/C6wH7LQIXy5/?img_index=1 www.tiktok.com/@remember_guy_simhi?_t=8kEXJJHWtwm&_r=1

In his memory, Shahar Gazenli wrote and composed the song "Come Back to Mom," available on YouTube. Some of its lyrics: "In wars no one wins / it's just who loses less / even the days have grown shorter / I struggle at night. // The truth is, the more time passes the more it hurts / the stars still paint your face / and without you the silence stabs / time does not stop / the tears / come back to Mom."

Hagar Yafe wrote the song "Guy's Hug": "Three in the morning, head up / I can't sleep, I came back from the party / I searched, I didn't find you there // For almost two weeks the skies / are so empty, I lost the melody / You left, and it left with you. // And how the pain doesn't pass / pills and piano into the night / and how the world doesn't collapse, the heart doesn't grasp it / and who will return to me your hug / yours, yours. // The city is silent, I have no peace anymore / suddenly you appear, wandering in my dreams / with that smile and those beautiful eyes. // And how the pain doesn't pass / pills and piano into the night / and how the world doesn't collapse, the heart doesn't grasp it / and who will return to me your hug / yours, yours. // Bye, Guy."
